title: Tungsten-free DRAM: ALD molybdenum wordlines plus Cu-Mn bitlines
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | buried-channel Si RCAT | voltage SA | planar 1T1C | CZ Si | thermal ALD + electroplating]: fill buried wordlines with liner-free ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2/H2 and replace W bitlines, contacts and periphery plugs with electroplated Cu wrapped in a self-forming MnSiOx barrier.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%): removes essentially all W from the flow; Mo comes largely from US/Chile copper by-product, and dropping the TiN liner cuts wordline resistance ~30% at 10 nm width.

title: Antimony-tin-oxide electrodes template rutile TiO2 high-k capacitors
idea: Box [rutile TiO2 cap, k~90 | Si access | voltage SA | pillar stack | CZ Si | thermal ALD]: use ALD SnO2:Sb, which is conductive and rutile-structured, as the bottom electrode so ALD TiO2 crystallizes directly as rutile below 400 C instead of low-k anatase; a 0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer at the top electrode suppresses leakage.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) plus Hf/Zr/Ru intensity: k~90 vs ~40 lets aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 to ~35:1 at equal Cs, halving deep-etch time and fluorocarbon use, with no Ru (the usual rutile template) and no Hf.

title: Porous-silicon lift-off wafers reuse one CZ parent fifty times
idea: Box [standard cell | Si access | voltage SA | thin device film bonded to handle | 30-50 um epi film | anodize + epi + bond + cleave]: anodize a double-porosity release layer on a premium CZ parent, grow device-grade epi from trichlorosilane, bond to a low-grade handle and cleave at the porous layer, then re-anodize the parent and repeat.
why: High-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%) and polysilicon: one CZ slice yields ~50 DRAM substrates, cutting HPQ crucible and poly consumption per wafer by roughly 10-30x.

title: Cold-crucible induction Czochralski growth with no quartz at all
idea: Box [standard 1T1C | Si access | voltage SA | standard | ingot pulled from a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with RF-levitated melt skull | magnetic CZ]: the melt touches only its own frozen Si skull, so no silica crucible and near-zero oxygen; nitrogen co-doping at 1e14-1e15 cm-3 replaces oxygen precipitates for intrinsic gettering.
why: Eliminates Spruce Pine HPQ crucible dependence outright and removes thermal-donor variability; RF energy rises ~20-30% per pull, but each $1-3k crucible and its supply risk disappear.

title: Indium-free, gallium-free ALD tin-oxide access transistors
idea: Box [stacked MIM cap | 4 nm ALD SnO2 vertical channel TFT | voltage SA | BEOL monolithic 1T1C over CMOS | logic wafer | thermal ALD]: replace IGZO with an ultrathin ALD SnO2 channel whose carrier density is set by oxygen-vacancy control and an O3 post-treatment, giving oxide-class off-current with only tin and oxygen.
why: Gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled) and indium chokepoints of oxide-semiconductor DRAM: keeps oxide-TFT ultra-low leakage (refresh cut >100x) while using tin from diversified sources.

title: Carbon-mold capacitors etched with oxygen instead of fluorocarbons
idea: Box [ZrO2 cylinder cap | Si access | voltage SA | pillar | CZ Si | O2/SO2 plasma + ash]: build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon with nitrogen-doped carbon support bands, etch the 70:1 holes with O2/SO2 instead of C4F6/C4F8 on oxide, deposit TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then ash the mold away (no HF wet strip).
why: PFAS/PFC intensity: oxide capacitor-hole etch is one of the largest fluorocarbon users (GWP 6,000-9,000); swapping it could cut fab PFC emissions ~20-30% and the carbon etch is faster.

title: Tool-level helium recapture loops with polymer membranes
idea: Box [helium lever: recapture | location: each etch chamber exhaust | purifier: PIM-1/polyimide membrane + small compressor | return: chuck supply line]: collect He from electrostatic-chuck backside leaks and leak-test exhaust, purify it to 5N at the tool and recycle it, buying cylinders only for makeup.
why: Helium (Qatar ~30% offline since March 2026): recovers ~80-90% of fab helium use and insulates DRAM output from the shortage; payback likely <2 years at current prices.

title: Urban-mined DRAM: re-binned retired DIMM dies in CXL expanders
idea: Box [existing DDR4 die | existing access | existing sense | CXL Type-3 expander | retired server DIMMs | test + retention re-binning]: route decommissioned hyperscale DIMMs to a test line that sorts dies by retention and bit-error rate, then a CXL controller with strong ECC and per-bin refresh tuning presents them as pooled far memory.
why: Raises usable memory supply with zero new wafers, crucibles, helium or tungsten; millions of retired DIMMs per year become a far-memory tier that offsets new DDR5 demand.

title: Panel-scale DRAM: oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on Gen-8.5 LCD glass
idea: Box [MIM cap | IGZO TFT | off-panel Si sense-amp chiplets | panel-level fan-out | 2.2x2.5 m glass | LCD-line photolithography]: fabricate relaxed-pitch (F~1 um) oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on idle, depreciated LCD lines, dice into tiles and flip-chip Si sense/periphery chiplets at panel level for a capacity tier.
why: Capital/EUV and crucible intensity: F=1 um gives ~16 Mb/cm2, so one 5.5 m2 panel holds ~100 GB with no EUV and no crystalline-Si array; low density limits it to slow capacity tiers.

title: Wurtzite ZnMgO ferroelectric capacitors replace hafnia and scandium
idea: Box [Zn0.6Mg0.4O ferroelectric polarization | Si access | charge sense with write-back | near-planar stacked cap | CZ Si | ALD/MOCVD]: use wurtzite zinc-magnesium oxide, whose ~80 uC/cm2 switchable polarization gives roughly 10x the signal charge of a 5 fF linear cap in a near-planar footprint.
why: Avoids Hf (HZO) and Sc (AlScN; scandium is China/Russia-dominated and very expensive); Zn and Mg are abundant and US-sourced, and a planar cell removes the high-AR etch; endurance is the open risk.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM using porosified p+ silicon sacrificial tiers
idea: Box [lateral cap | lateral Si access per tier | voltage SA | 3D stacked tiers | CZ Si | all-Si epi + electrochemical porosification]: grow alternating p++ (B 1e20) and lightly doped Si epi tiers instead of Si/SiGe, then after slit etch anodize only the p++ layers into porous Si and remove them laterally, leaving suspended single-crystal channels.
why: Removes germane/Ge (China dominates refined Ge, export-licensed since 2023) from 3D DRAM, and avoids the SiGe strain-relaxation cap on tier count so >100 tiers become possible.

title: Silicon-carbide access transistors make DRAM cells nearly non-leaking
idea: Box [MIM cap | 4H-SiC trench MOSFET (3.26 eV gap) | Si voltage SA | array-on-periphery hybrid bond | 200 mm SiC wafers from the EV supply chain | DUV litho]: build the cell array on SiC, where intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm-3 versus 1e10 for Si, so junction and GIDL leakage collapse, then bond it onto a Si periphery wafer.
why: Leakage tail/refresh (~46 fJ/bit): retention goes from 64 ms toward hours, refresh nearly vanishes and Cs can drop to ~1 fF (shallower caps, less ZrO2/TiN/etch gas); uses fast-growing US SiC wafer capacity instead of HPQ-crucible CZ.

title: Ceria-free, slurry-free planarization by photo-cured resin etch-back
idea: Box [any cell | any access | any sense | any | Si | spin-on self-leveling resin + UV-ozone conversion + uniform dry etch-back]: replace CeO2-slurry oxide CMP steps (STI, capacitor top, ILD) with a self-leveling photo-curable siloxane resin that is converted to SiO2 by UV-ozone and etched back 1:1 to the stop layer.
why: Cerium (rare earth, China-dominated refining) and water: removes 6-10 CMP steps per DRAM flow, together with their slurry waste and a large share of rinse UPW.

title: ALD alumina nano-topcoat replaces fluorinated immersion-litho topcoats
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | ArF immersion]: after resist coat, grow 2-3 nm of 60 C ALD Al2O3 from TMA/H2O as the leach barrier, cap it with a fluorine-free hydrocarbon monolayer for water receding angle, and let the TMAH developer dissolve it.
why: PFAS: immersion topcoats and topcoat-free additives are fluorinated and face EU restriction; removes fluorinated chemistry from ~10-15 immersion layers per DRAM flow.

title: Display-scrap indium and gallium loop feeding oxide-semiconductor memory
idea: Box [feedstock: spent IGZO sputter targets + end-of-life panels | refining: acid leach + solvent extraction | product: targets and ALD precursors | buyer: BEOL oxide-memory fabs]: contract recyclers to recover In/Ga from spent targets (only ~30% of a target is consumed) and scrapped panels, and recast them as dedicated memory-grade feedstock.
why: In/Ga chokepoints (China ~60% In, ~98% Ga): spent targets alone return ~70% of purchased indium, securing feedstock if oxide-semiconductor DRAM scales.

title: DNA-origami masks pattern sub-10 nm capacitor arrays without EUV
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | Si access | voltage SA | standard | Si | DNA-origami self-assembly on coarse docking sites + silica mineralization]: dock origami tiles carrying a programmed honeycomb of 8 nm openings onto DUV-defined sites, mineralize them with DNA-templated sol-gel silica into a hard mask, and transfer the hole array into the capacitor mold.
why: EUV single supplier and 5-7 EUV layers: replaces 2-3 capacitor/contact EUV layers with room-temperature biochemistry; DNA synthesis cost has fallen by orders of magnitude.

title: Reclaim end-of-life solar silicon as purified DRAM polysilicon feed
idea: Box [feedstock: retired PV cells | purification: hydrochlorination to trichlorosilane | deposition: US Siemens reactors | product: 11N poly for CZ]: delaminate retired modules, strip Ag/Al from the 5-6N cells, convert the silicon to trichlorosilane and re-deposit electronic-grade polysilicon.
why: Polysilicon concentration and energy: PV waste reaches millions of tonnes in the 2030s; recycled feed skips carbothermic reduction and diversifies a China-heavy supply chain.

title: Socketed design-for-disassembly DRAM packages for multi-life reuse
idea: Box [standard die | standard | standard | compression-interposer LGA packages on CAMM/CXL boards | n/a | solderless assembly]: standardize DRAM packages that mount without solder and carry an on-package wear/retention log, so dies move from retired boards to new controller generations.
why: Raises usable supply per fabbed bit: stretching DRAM service life from ~5 to ~10 years through reuse could halve new-bit demand for capacity tiers, with no solder-rework yield loss.

title: Proton-electrolyte double-layer storage node multiplies capacitance per area
idea: Box [electric double layer in 3 nm phosphosilicate proton conductor | Si access | voltage SA | near-planar | CZ Si | ALD/sol-gel]: replace the high-AR dielectric capacitor with an electrode / proton-conducting glass / blocking-electrode stack where protons pile up within ~1 nm of the electrode, giving ~10-20 uF/cm2 versus ~4 uF/cm2 for ZrO2.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 3-5x areal capacitance could let an AR ~15 capacitor reach 5 fF with no hafnia/zirconia and no deep etch; ion response must beat 10 ns, which is the big unknown.

title: Zero-liquid-discharge water loop using fab waste-heat membrane distillation
idea: Box [water source: RO reject + CMP/wet-bench rinse | heat source: 30-60 C process-cooling return | unit: membrane distillation + crystallizer | output: UPW feed]: recover >95% of reject water using heat the fab already throws away and crystallize the salts.
why: Water intensity: cuts net fab water withdrawal >80%, which makes DRAM fabs siteable in arid US states (AZ, TX, NM).

title: Hafnium-free periphery: array bonded onto mature SiON-poly CMOS wafer
idea: Box [standard 1T1C array | Si access | sense amps on bottom wafer | Cu-Cu hybrid-bonded CMOS-bonded-array | array wafer + 28-40 nm SiON/poly periphery wafer | split fab]: build sense amps and decoders on a mature node with no HfO2/La high-k metal gate and no EUV, then bond the array wafer on top.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die and DRAM's only HKMG/Hf user: moves half the die to depreciated, EUV-free tools and removes Hf/La from DRAM while shrinking the array die ~40%.

title: 2T1C cell with in-cell preamp shrinks capacitor to 1 fF stub
idea: Box [1 fF stub cap, AR ~12:1 | Si access + stacked vertical oxide-TFT read transistor | current sense | monolithic | CZ Si | standard]: the storage node both holds charge on a short capacitor and gates a stacked read transistor, so readout is non-destructive current rather than charge sharing.
why: Capacitor charge wall and materials: AR 70:1 drops to ~12:1, cutting mold-etch fluorocarbons and ALD precursor per bit ~5x and removing destructive-read write-back energy.

title: Cold-trap recapture and re-purification of unreacted ALD precursors
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | any | ALD]: insert a condensation trap plus sorbent bed between each ALD chamber and pump to capture the Zr/Hf/Ti amide and Al alkyl precursor that passes unreacted, then redistill it centrally and requalify it by NMR and ICP-MS.
why: Hf/Zr/Ti precursor and energy intensity: ALD precursor utilization is often <10%, so recapture could cut precursor purchases ~5x for the high-k steps that dominate DRAM ALD.

title: Nanoimprint plus block-copolymer DSA prints DRAM arrays without excimer lasers
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | buried-WL Si | voltage SA | standard | CZ Si | jet-and-flash NIL cured by 365 nm LEDs + PS-b-PMMA DSA annealed in N2 + O2/HBr/N2 transfer etch with no Ar dilution]: imprint guide patterns at 2x pitch from e-beam-written masters, then let the block copolymer split them into 12 nm honeycomb holes and lines.
why: Neon (ArF laser buffer gas) and EUV (whose CO2 drive laser runs on a helium mix): removes all array-layer excimer and EUV exposures; NIL tool capex is ~1/4 of EUV and power ~1/10.

title: Solid-state 213 nm laser steppers replace neon-buffered ArF excimers
idea: Box [standard | standard | standard | standard | Si | DUV projection lithography with fifth-harmonic diode-pumped Nd:YAG (213 nm) source]: generate DUV in CLBO/KBBF nonlinear crystals instead of an Ar/F2/Ne gas discharge, and re-coat 193 nm-class optics for 213 nm.
why: Neon (about half once came from Ukraine) and krypton/fluorine gas logistics: zero rare-gas consumables and longer source life; reaching ~100 W average power is the hurdle.

title: Maskless four-beam interference lithography for periodic DRAM cell arrays
idea: Box [honeycomb cap array | buried WL | voltage SA | standard | Si | immersion four-beam interference from a 266 nm solid-state laser + spacer doubling]: because the cell array is perfectly periodic, expose its holes and gratings with interfering beams (~46 nm half-pitch, no mask, no projection lens), halve the pitch with spacers, and trim array edges with a coarse LED block exposure.
why: Removes rare-gas light sources and masks for ~5 array layers; an interference tool costs maybe 1/20 of an EUV scanner.

title: Sputter-free fab: every liner, barrier and electrode by thermal ALD
idea: Box [ALD TiN/ZrO2 cap | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | thermal ALD/CVD with N2 carriers + NH3/H2 reducers + remote NH3/NF3 pre-clean]: requalify every Ar-sputtered film (Ti/TiN contact liners, bitline metal, silicide seed, periphery gate metal) and every Ar sputter pre-clean as gas-phase thermal processes.
why: Removes argon from deposition entirely; the constraint also forces near-100% step coverage, which 3D DRAM tiers and high-AR contacts need anyway.

title: Gasless sustained self-sputtering ignited by a hydrogen pulse
idea: Box [Cu bitline / Ti liner | n/a | n/a | n/a | Si | HiPIMS sustained self-sputtering]: strike the magnetron with a 10 us H2 pulse, then keep the plasma alive purely on ionized target metal at >1 kW/cm2 peak power, giving a fully ionized, directional metal flux with zero working gas.
why: Removes Ar from metal PVD while improving bottom coverage in 60:1 features through ion-directed deposition, and eliminates trapped-Ar voids in films.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: Box [MIS trench cap in bulk Si | vertical Si access | voltage SA | revived trench-capacitor 1T1C | CZ Si | NIL-patterned electroless Ag mesh + HF/H2O2 metal-assisted chemical etch]: the Ag catalyst sinks vertically in the HF/H2O2 bath, cutting 30 nm holes at >150:1 aspect ratio with no plasma; the holes are then lined with ALD dielectric and doped poly.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs AR ~115): a wet, room-temperature etch reaches AR 150+ with almost no tool capex, replacing high-AR plasma etchers that need Ar/He dilution and backside cooling; the Ag is recovered from the bath.

title: Anodic alumina nanopore templates host ultra-high-aspect capacitor arrays
idea: Box [MIM cap in anodic alumina pores | Si access below | voltage SA | capacitor layer over storage contacts | e-beam-evaporated Al film (vacuum, no gas) | two-step oxalic-acid anodization guided by NIL dimples]: anodize a 3 um Al film into self-ordered 25-40 nm pores registered to imprinted dimples, wet-open the barrier oxide, and deposit TiN/dielectric/TiN inside.
why: Capacitor charge wall and etch intensity: AR 100-200 holes cost about as much as a plating bath, with no fluorocarbon etch and no rare gases; Al is abundant and US-made.

title: Hydrogen-ambient Czochralski pulling in silicon-nitride crucibles
idea: Box [standard | standard | standard | standard | 300 mm CZ Si under recycled low-pressure H2 | Si3N4-coated SiC crucible + magnetic CZ]: sweep SiO and CO from the puller with H2 instead of argon (its higher thermal conductivity allows faster pulling) and hold the melt in a nitride-faced crucible that releases nitrogen, useful for void control, rather than oxygen.
why: Removes both the argon purge and the Spruce Pine HPQ crucible from wafer making; H2 heat extraction might raise pull rate ~10-20%.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in etch and deposition chucks
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | electrostatic-chuck backside gas = 5-15 Torr H2 in a closed loop]: H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), so swap the chuck backside gas to H2 below flammability limits, with Pd-membrane return and O2 interlocks.
why: Helium (Qatar offline): backside cooling is a dominant fab He use; H2 matches or beats wafer temperature uniformity at a small fraction of the price and is made on site.

title: On-site electrolytic hydrogen and nitrogen as the fab's only inerts
idea: Box [supply: PEM electrolyzers on reclaimed water + PSA N2 generators | uses: load-lock venting, carrier gas, PECVD dilution | leak test: 5% H2-in-N2 tracer with Pd-gate sniffers | storage: no rare-gas cylinders on site]: redesign the fab gas plant so N2 and H2 cover every inert role, and send the electrolytic O2 by-product to ozone generators.
why: Removes all He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe supply exposure for a DRAM fab using US-manufacturable equipment and renewable power.

title: Slot-die sol-gel zinc-tin-oxide gain cells patterned on logic BEOL
idea: Box [charge on read-TFT gate | 2T0C ZnSnO TFTs | current sense | BEOL monolithic over CMOS | logic wafer | aqueous nitrate sol-gel slot-die coat + NIL patterning + 265 nm UV-LED assisted 300 C cure in air]: coat ZnSnO channel and AlOx gate-dielectric inks at atmospheric pressure, with no vacuum, no sputter targets and no lamps.
why: Ga/In-free (Zn and Sn are abundant) and sputter-free oxide gain cells: leakage <1e-18 A gives seconds of retention, so refresh falls ~100x, with no IGZO targets or Ar plasma.

title: Bistable buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams as non-volatile DRAM cells
idea: Box [mechanical state of a pre-buckled 300 nm SiN beam | electrostatic pull-in hysteresis, self-selecting with no transistor | capacitive sense of up/down state | BEOL cavity array | Si | LPCVD SiN from DCS+NH3 + vapor-HF/ethanol release in N2]: snap a compressively stressed nanobeam between two stable states with a 10 ns pulse; GHz beam frequencies allow 5-20 ns switching and non-contact snapping avoids wear.
why: Materials: a cell built only from Si and N, with no high-k, W, Hf or oxide semiconductor, and no refresh; endurance and density are the open risks.

title: Electroplated NiFe/Cu multilayer nanowires as cobalt-free magnetic RAM
idea: Box [NiFe/Cu/NiFe CPP-GMR pseudo-spin-valve | Si access transistor | resistive sense at ~10-15% GMR | BEOL vias as templates | Si | pulsed single-bath electrodeposition]: alternate the plating potential to stack ferromagnetic and spacer layers inside 20 nm vias and switch the soft layer by spin-transfer torque.
why: MRAM normally needs Ar-sputtered CoFeB/MgO plus Pt/Ir/Ru seeds and Co; this uses only Ni, Fe and Cu at room temperature without vacuum; magnetic endurance is unlimited, but low GMR slows sensing to ~20-30 ns.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal trims the access-transistor leakage tail
idea: Box [standard cap | Si access with deuterium-passivated gate oxide and junction | standard | standard | Si | 10-20 atm D2 anneal at 400 C replacing Ar/forming-gas anneals]: Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation ~10x better than Si-H, so the trap sites behind trap-assisted GIDL stay passivated.
why: Leakage tail (13 fA) and refresh energy: pushing tail retention out 2-4x lets the refresh interval double or quadruple, roughly halving refresh power (16-33% of idle), using D2 rather than any rare gas.

title: Supercritical CO2 and ozone dry cleaning replaces most UPW rinses
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | single-wafer scCO2 + co-solvent + dissolved O3 cleaner with CO2 recompression loop]: strip post-etch residue and particles inside high-AR capacitor holes with supercritical CO2, which has no surface tension and so causes no pattern collapse, recovering >95% of the CO2.
why: Water and pattern collapse at AR 70+: could cut wet-clean UPW ~50-70%, eliminate IPA drying and allow taller capacitors without stiction.

title: Monolayer doping forms damage-free access-transistor junctions
idea: Box [standard cap | RCAT Si with molecular-monolayer-doped junctions | standard | standard | Si | allylboronic or allylphosphonate SAM + oxide cap + N2 spike anneal]: replace beamline implants at the storage-node junction with self-assembled dopant molecules driven in by RTP, giving abrupt sub-5 nm junctions with no implant point defects.
why: Implant damage seeds the trap-assisted leakage tail; damage-free junctions could cut tail GIDL ~3-10x, which means less refresh, and remove implanter plasma-flood gas use.

title: UV-LED retrofit kits strip rare-gas lamps from legacy steppers
idea: Box [product: drop-in 365/385 nm LED illuminator | target: installed i-line steppers | layers: non-critical DRAM masks (implant blocks, pads, periphery) | model: per-layer service fee]: replace Hg arc lamps, whose bulbs carry Xe/Ar fill, with long-life LED arrays that switch instantly.
why: Removes rare-gas consumables and mercury from the ~30-40% of DRAM mask layers that are non-critical and cuts their litho energy ~60%; also sells to 200 mm fabs.

title: Green DPSS laser zone-melting builds single-crystal tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: Box [lateral cap | crystalline-Si transistor per tier | voltage SA | monolithic 3D tiers | deposited a-Si on SiO2 with Si seed vias | 532 nm diode-pumped laser lateral zone melt in vacuum]: melt each deposited a-Si tier in narrow scanning lines that carry crystal orientation laterally out of the seed vias, giving near-single-crystal islands with no excimer (XeCl) laser and no epi.
why: 3D DRAM needs 26+ crystalline tiers: this avoids SiGe/Ge epi superlattices and rare-gas excimer lasers, at a per-tier cost of one laser scan.

title: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled DRAM pools shrink capacitors fivefold
idea: Box [1 fF stub cap, AR ~15:1 | Si access at 77 K | low-noise voltage SA | LN2-immersion rack shared over CXL | Si | standard]: at 77 K, subthreshold and junction leakage fall by >1e6, so retention exceeds hours and 1 fF suffices; cooling uses LN2 from air separation, which needs no helium (unlike sub-20 K cryogenics).
why: Capacitor wall, refresh and materials: ~5x less capacitor stack, near-zero refresh, and ~5x lower Cu wire resistance; the cryocooler overhead means it pays off only for dense pooled racks.

title: Calcium titanate perovskite capacitors from earth-abundant elements
idea: Box [CaTiO3 (k~150) cap | Si access | voltage SA | pillar | Si | thermal ALD from a Ca cyclopentadienyl + Ti amide + O3 with N2 purges]: grow perovskite CaTiO3 on a conductive Nb:TiO2 bottom electrode that seeds crystallization near 450 C, with no Sr, Ru or Hf.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) and scarce-element intensity: Ca and Ti are abundant and US-available, and k~150 lets AR fall to ~25:1; crystallization temperature and leakage are the risks.

title: Electroless nickel-boron electrodes coat 100:1 capacitor holes conformally
idea: Box [MIM cap with Ni-B electrodes | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | autocatalytic electroless deposition after molecular Sn/Ag activation]: seed the hole walls, grow 3 nm Ni-B autocatalytically (self-limiting by bath depletion), then nitridize its surface with NH3 for a stable interface to the dielectric.
why: Replaces slow TiCl4/NH3 ALD TiN with a wet, room-temperature process that is conformal at any aspect ratio, needs no vacuum or rare gases, and uses broadly sourced Ni.

title: Water-vapor plasma activated hybrid bonding for HBM stacks
idea: Box [HBM DRAM dies | standard | standard | bumpless Cu-SiCN hybrid-bonded HBM | Si | H2O/N2 low-power plasma activation + formic-acid vapor Cu-oxide reduction + 250 C anneal]: hydroxyl-terminate the SiCN with water-vapor plasma and reduce Cu oxide chemically instead of using Ar/N2 plasma activation or Ar sputter cleaning.
why: HBM TSV/microbump tax (3x area, 20-30% yield loss): bumpless bonding cuts pitch ~10x and removes underfill, with no argon in the flow.

title: CHIPS tranche paying per kilogram of rare gas designed out
idea: Box [lever: federal memory incentive | metric: kg He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe avoided per wafer | verification: tool-level mass-flow logging | kicker: guaranteed DoD offtake for certified rare-gas-free memory]: pay fabs per audited kilogram of rare gas eliminated and give certified flows priority procurement.
why: U.S. manufacturability and helium/neon chokepoints: turns supply risk into an investable metric that pulls NIL, H2 cooling and solid-state lasers into DRAM fabs.
